author: b. e. kaiser
title: Scott Gray discusses medical center updates and park funding after Albany budget hearings - North Country Leader
text:
Assemblyman Scott Gray (R-Watertown) has released a new episode of his video series, “The Gray Area,” providing updates on the Claxton-Hepburn Medical Center and recent state budget hearings in Albany.
Gray stated that progress is being made regarding the Claxton-Hepburn Medical Center and the North Star Health Alliance, with efforts underway to stabilize operations at these institutions. He did not provide specific details but indicated that work continues toward stability.
During ongoing state budget hearings in Albany, Gray emphasized the need for further investment in parks within his district. As a member of the Committee on Tourism, Parks, Arts and Sports Development, he advocated for increased funding for local parks.
“This week in Albany, we made great progress in securing funding for our state parks in the state budget,” said Gray. “The 116th Assembly District is home to 28 state parks, and my goal is to ensure that each one receives adequate funding to ensure North Country residents and visitors can enjoy our state parks, which contributes to the tourism economy.”
Gray also serves on the Committee on Energy. He questioned the Public Service Commission Chair about recent utility rate increases. According to Gray, electricity bills have risen by over 33% across New York over the past decade.
“Every year, North Country residents watch their utility rates climb higher and higher without any explanation or acknowledgment by regulators,” said Gray. “I was disappointed to hear the Public Service Commission Chair excuse away these dramatic rate increases. Working families deserve transparency, and that’s exactly what I’ll continue to fight for as your voice in Albany.”
In addition to legislative activities, Gray met with various advocacy groups during visits this week at Albany’s Capitol. Groups included 1199 SEIU and Cornell Cooperative Extension who discussed their priorities ahead of finalizing the next state budget.
“Look out for next week’s episode of The Gray Area as we continue to update you on what you care about. We always appreciate the opportunity to serve you and to work with you. Don’t hesitate to call my office staff with questions, comments or concerns; see you soon,” Gray concluded.
Scott Gray represents parts of Jefferson and St. Lawrence counties in the New York State Assembly according to his official biography. His legislative focus includes job creation initiatives as well as policies supporting agriculture and tourism and promoting community safety. Previously he served as chairman of the Jefferson County Board of Legislators and is a fourth-generation business owner from Watertown.
